intro.title: PathFindingVisualizer Project Overview
intro.desc: PathFindingVisualizer is a project page skeleton for a pathfinding algorithm visualizer. It follows the same structure as the other project pages, so demos, architecture notes, and code snippets can be added consistently later.

text: This page is prepared as the base documentation structure for the PathFindingVisualizer project.
The project will focus on visualizing grid-based search and pathfinding behavior, including visited nodes, frontier expansion, obstacle handling, and final path reconstruction.
After the first stable milestone, I will add demo media, algorithm diagrams, and selected code snippets for the core search pipeline.

basic_demo.title: Basic Demo
basic_demo.desc: Shows the core search flow from board setup to final path reconstruction.

step_controls.title: Step Controls
step_controls.desc: Shows stepping forward and backward through the simulation history.

speed_control.title: Speed Control
speed_control.desc: Shows how auto-run speed affects the pacing of the visualization.

weights_algorithms.title: Weights and Algorithms
weights_algorithms.desc: Shows how different weights and algorithm choices change the explored path.

code_summaries.simulation_controller_step_history: SimulationController handles auto-run pacing, single-step progression, history snapshots, undo recovery, and final statistics as the scheduler between algorithm execution and board visualization.
code_summaries.pathfinder_shared_helpers: The Pathfinder base class centralizes shared board access, movement cost, heuristic computation, tile-state markers, and parent-chain reconstruction so each algorithm does not repeat visualization logic.
code_summaries.a_star_visual_step: A* advances one visual step at a time: pop the current best node, relax neighbors, and update best-cost, parent links, G/H/F values, and Open/Current state.
code_summaries.board_neighbors_and_cost: Board owns neighbor filtering, diagonal-policy checks, weighted movement cost, and final path statistics, giving algorithms a unified interface for legal movement.

module_architecture.title: Module Architecture
module_architecture.desc: Shows the responsibility boundaries between Application, SimulationController, Pathfinder, Board, and Tile.

step_sequence.title: Step and Undo Sequence
step_sequence.desc: Shows how Next Step and Auto Run save snapshots, advance the algorithm, update statistics, and support Prev Step.

search_data_flow.title: Search Data Flow
search_data_flow.desc: Shows the data flow between start/goal nodes, neighbors, costs, parent chains, and the final path during a visualized search step.
